newsitem.title: INDIA: State stays key financer in Asia core sector -ADB.
newsitem.headline: State stays key financer in Asia core sector -ADB.

text.p: Private funds are seen as the answer to Asia's growing need for financing core sector projects but governments will continue to contribute the lion's share, a senior Asian Development Bank (ADB) official said on Wednesday.

"The private sector is increasingly been seen as the answer that will satisfy Asia's hunger for infrastructure finance, meet the growing shortfall of Official Development Assistance from abroad and come to the rescue of the public sector," said Bong-Suh Lee, ADB's vice president (West).
He said the private sector had so far contributed just 10 percent of the region's total expenditure in infrastructure development.

"It comes as no surprise that the pressure is rising to increase this share substantially, considering that annual spending by developing Asia in infrastructure in the next 10 years is expected to rise from less than 5 percent to 7 percent of rapidly increasing GDP," Lee said.
Half of the incremental investment would be financed by the private sector taking its contribution up to 20 percent of total expenditure, he said.
"Even with the scenario of increased private sector participation, some 80 percent of infrastructure development will still be in the hands of the public sector," Lee said.
He said the public sector must increase its efficiency and provide a conducive environment for private investment.
